key_insight: The paper shows that discrete log-concavity of the ground state is the structural bridge that lets adiabatic quantum optimization capture tunneling benefits for a much broader class of convex and mildly spiky potentials.
engineering_relevance: This extends the design space for AQO problem Hamiltonians beyond exactly solvable cases, suggesting more realistic convex optimization landscapes may still admit provable tunneling-based speedups.
method: Proves a framework for discrete log-concavity of ground states in a family of 1D discrete Schrödinger operators.
Uses log-concavity to derive new spectral gap bounds for convex potentials, improving on prior convex-potential results.
Extends Reichardt-style perturbative tunneling analysis from the Hamming-weight-with-a-spike model to log-concave-ground-state potentials, including a quadratic spike case.
evidence_signal: The paper reports theoretical results and an extension of analysis from a linear, exactly solvable potential to a quadratic, non-solvable potential, indicating broader analytical coverage rather than empirical benchmarking.
watch_item: The results are still theoretical and hinge on special structural assumptions such as discrete 1D settings and log-concave ground states, so direct hardware performance gains are not yet demonstrated.
paper_title: Log-concavity and tunneling: adiabatic quantum optimization for convex functions (with a spike)
